alt: Sold as the Dodge Ram 2500 through the 2010 model year

issues.t: Loose timing-case dowel pin ("killer dowel pin")
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In the worst case a sudden loud clatter or grinding from the front of the engine, followed by the engine quitting.
issues.why: A small alignment pin pressed into the front of the block behind the timing cover can work loose from vibration and fall into the timing gears.
issues.next: If the pin has never been secured, have a diesel shop install a retaining tab kit. Shut the engine off right away if you hear new grinding from the front.

issues.t: 47RE automatic slipping or losing overdrive
issues.sym: Slipping under load, late or soft shifts, shudder when the converter locks, or no overdrive, especially when towing.
issues.why: The 47RE four-speed automatic is marginal behind the Cummins torque. Heavy towing and heat wear the overdrive band, clutches and converter.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the transmission looked at early. Avoid heavy towing until it is fixed, since slipping builds heat and speeds up the damage.

issues.t: VP44 injection pump failure (weak lift pump)
issues.sym: Hard starting, rough or surging idle, sudden loss of power or the engine dying while driving, often with a fuel-related trouble code.
issues.why: The electronic VP44 injection pump is cooled and lubricated by the fuel it gets from the lift pump. When the factory lift pump weakens, the injection pump runs starved and hot and fails.
issues.next: Have fuel supply pressure tested. Fix a weak lift pump before or along with any injection pump work. Tow the truck in if it stalls and will not restart.

issues.t: Cracked "53" engine block
issues.sym: Slow coolant loss, a damp spot or seepage on the passenger side of the block, white smoke or overheating.
issues.why: Some blocks from this period, marked with a "53" casting number on the driver side, have thin water jacket walls that can crack, especially with towing, added power or overheating.
issues.next: Stop driving if it is overheating. Have a diesel shop confirm the casting number and pressure-test the cooling system if coolant keeps disappearing.

issues.t: Violent front-end shake ("death wobble") from worn front-end parts
issues.sym: Hard side-to-side shaking of the steering wheel and front end after hitting a bump at speed, or loose, wandering steering.
issues.why: The solid front axle relies on the track bar, tie rods, drag link, ball joints and steering damper. Wear or looseness in any of them, and quick-wearing ball joints on early trucks, can start the shake.
issues.next: Slow down gently and pull over when it happens. Have the whole front end inspected for play before driving far, and check the VIN for open steering recalls.

issues.t: 48RE automatic slipping, shudder or overdrive failure
issues.sym: Slipping, flare between gears, converter shudder or loss of overdrive, usually worse when towing or after added power.
issues.why: The 48RE is an updated four-speed but still works hard behind the diesel. Heat and load wear the bands, clutches and converter.
issues.next: Keep the fluid fresh and full and have shifting problems checked early. Ease off heavy towing until it is diagnosed.

issues.t: Common-rail fuel injector wear
issues.sym: Rough idle, extra smoke, a knocking or cackling sound, harder starting and lower fuel mileage.
issues.why: On the common-rail 5.9, injector nozzles and seats wear with mileage and dirty fuel, so they leak or spray poorly.
issues.next: Have a diesel shop run an injector return-flow test. Changing fuel filters on schedule helps the injectors last.

issues.t: EGR cooler leaking coolant into the engine
issues.sym: White exhaust smoke with a sweet smell, coolant level dropping with no outside leak, or pressure in the coolant overflow tank.
issues.why: Heat cycling and soot buildup fatigue the cooler that chills recirculated exhaust gas. Once it cracks inside, coolant is drawn into the intake.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it checked if you see sweet-smelling white smoke and coolant loss. Coolant in the cylinders can badly damage the engine.

issues.t: Diesel particulate filter clogging and fuel in the oil
issues.sym: Frequent cleaning cycles, a reduced-power mode, poor mileage, filter warning messages, or the oil level rising.
issues.why: Short trips and lots of idling stop the filter from burning off soot. The extra fuel used during cleaning cycles can wash into the oil on these early trucks.
issues.next: Give the truck regular longer drives, check the oil level often, and have filter warnings looked at before the truck goes into limp mode.

issues.t: Variable-geometry turbo sticking
issues.sym: Low power, a boost-related code, whistling or grinding from the turbo, or a weak exhaust brake.
issues.why: Soot builds up on the turbo vanes and their ring so they bind, and the electronic actuator that moves them can wear out.
issues.next: Have the turbo and actuator diagnosed. Cleaning the vanes sometimes fixes it before a replacement is needed.

issues.t: Intake heater grid bolt can loosen and fall into the engine
issues.sym: Often no warning before it fails. Sometimes hard cold starts. If the bolt drops in, sudden knocking and severe engine damage.
issues.why: The grid heater that warms intake air for cold starts is held by internal fasteners that loosen from heat, soot and corrosion over many miles.
issues.next: Ask a diesel shop to check the grid heater for looseness at service time on higher-mileage trucks. Stop the engine at once if a sudden knock appears.

issues.t: DEF / SCR system faults and NOx sensor failures
issues.sym: Emissions warnings, a countdown to reduced speed, erratic DEF gauge readings, white crystals around the dosing parts, or heater faults in winter.
issues.why: The exhaust fluid system can be upset by contaminated or old fluid, crystal buildup in the pump or doser, and failing heaters or NOx sensors.
issues.next: Use fresh, sealed DEF and have warnings checked before the speed limit kicks in.

issues.t: Drag link nut can loosen (recall 19V-021)
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, clunking, or a sudden loss of steering if the link separates.
issues.why: A jam nut on the steering drag link adjuster may not hold, letting one end of the link separate.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it done right away. Have any new steering looseness inspected before driving.

issues.t: Hemi lifter and camshaft wear
issues.sym: A steady ticking or tapping from the engine, then misfires, a rough idle and a check-engine light.
issues.why: Roller lifters can stop rolling and wear flat, then grind down the camshaft lobes. It is widely reported and the subject of a class action lawsuit.
issues.next: Have a ticking Hemi checked promptly; catching it early limits the damage. Use the correct oil and change it on time.

issues.t: CP4 high-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Hard starting, loss of power or the engine shutting off while driving, sometimes with low fuel pressure codes.
issues.why: The CP4 pump used for these two years can wear internally and send metal through the whole fuel system. Ram went back to the older CP3 pump for 2021.
issues.next: Drain the water separator and change fuel filters on time. Tow the truck in if it stalls; metal in the filter means the whole fuel system needs inspection.

issues.t: Wheel speed sensor faults (TSB 05-004-24)
issues.sym: ABS, traction control or brake warning lights coming on, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: Wheel speed sensor faults are a known issue on these trucks, and Ram issued a service bulletin for them.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about TSB 05-004-24. ABS and stability control may not work while the light is on.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag inflator may rupture (recall 25V-824)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The problem shows up only if the curtain airbag deploys.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect may let the side curtain airbag inflator rupture during deployment.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the repair as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Transmission fluid can spray from the dipstick tube (recall 22V-835)
issues.sym: A hot oil smell or smoke from under the truck after hard driving or towing, and wet fluid near the dipstick tube.
issues.why: On the 68RFE six-speed automatic, heat and pressure can push fluid out of the dipstick tube onto hot parts, creating a fire risk and lowering the fluid level.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the fluid level checked. Pull over and shut off the engine if you see smoke.

issues.t: Intake air heater relay can short and start a fire (recalls 21V-163, 21V-798)
issues.sym: A burning electrical smell or smoke from under the hood, even with the truck parked and off.
issues.why: The relay that powers the intake air heater for cold starts can short internally and overheat.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for open recalls right away. Until the fix is done, park outside and away from buildings and other vehicles.

issues.t: Software may let speed exceed the tire rating (recall 26V-288)
issues.sym: No warning signs; the truck may allow higher top speeds than its tires are rated for.
issues.why: A powertrain control software error may not limit top speed to match the tires fitted, raising the risk of tire failure at very high speed.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the software update. Stay within legal speeds until it is done.

issues.t: Rearview camera may not display (recall 26V-327)
issues.sym: A blank or missing backup camera image when shifting into reverse.
issues.why: Contamination or incorrect programming in the camera processing module can stop the image from showing.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Back up with extra care using mirrors until it is fixed.

issues.t: Instrument cluster display can go blank (recalls 25V-826, 26V-225)
issues.sym: The gauge cluster screen goes dark, so speed and warning lights are not shown.
issues.why: Software errors in the instrument cluster can make the display fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check the VIN for these recalls and get the update. If the cluster goes blank, pull over safely and have it fixed before driving on.

issues.t: Trailer lights and trailer brakes may fail (recall 26V-059)
issues.sym: Trailer brake lights, turn signals or trailer brakes stop working while towing.
issues.why: A faulty trailer tow module can cut power to trailer lighting and the electric trailer brake controller.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Do not tow until the trailer tow module has been replaced if your truck is included.

issues.t: Airbag and stability control software error (recall 25V-882)
issues.sym: Possible airbag or stability control warning lights; often no warning at all.
issues.why: A software error in the occupant restraint controller may keep the driver airbag or seat belt pretensioner from firing and can switch off stability control.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the update right away.

issues.t: Steering column module may disable stability control (recalls 26V-244, 26V-651)
issues.sym: Stability control warnings, or stability control not working.
issues.why: A fault in the steering column control module can cause a loss of electronic stability control.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and have the module replaced. Drive with extra care on slippery roads until it is done.

issues.t: Dashboard top cracks and crumbles
issues.sym: Long splits open across the top of the dash, usually starting near the defroster vents and the passenger airbag line, and the edges break away into loose pieces.
issues.why: The hard plastic dash panel of these trucks goes brittle in sunlight and heat, so it splits along its moulded seams once it ages.
issues.next: Cosmetic, but have broken pieces secured or fitted with a cover so nothing rattles loose over the airbag or falls into the defroster vents.
